lessons.name: AN OBSTRUCTION AT MODULUS 26, REDUCED EXPONENT 2. So x^n + y^n = z^n has NO solution in integers with x, y, z all coprime to 26, for EVERY exponent n reducing to 2 — that is n in [10,14,22] of the range walked, and every larger n with the same gcd against 12. An unbounded conclusion from a finite table. It settles the coprime case only — classically Case I — and infinitely many triples sharing a factor with 26 pass through untouched, so the coprime half is what it decides and the other half is untouched.

It settles the coprime case only — classically Case I — and infinitely many triples sharing a factor with 110 pass through untouched, so the coprime half is what it decides and the other half is untouched.
